record.summary: Apart from the three accepted deviations, the render matches the reference: the rail, the header, the Appearance card and the Navigation card show the same content, layout and states.

accepted_deviations.as_given: Text size: the control is disabled (muted labels) and its line under it says "Coming soon" in place of "Scales the whole app: Small 87.5 %, Default 100 %, Large 112.5 %." (step D adds text size later). On a narrow screen the one-line note makes every section below it sit about one text line higher.
accepted_deviations.note: The Small / Default / Large segments are muted and the note under them reads "Coming soon". At this desktop width both notes take one line, so the Navigation card starts at the same height in both pictures.

accepted_deviations.as_given: A new "NOTIFICATIONS" section with one "Notifications" switch (off) sits between the Navigation section and the New chat defaults section. So New chat defaults sits lower, or below the bottom edge.
accepted_deviations.note: The NOTIFICATIONS card with a "Notifications" switch (off) starts where NEW CHAT DEFAULTS starts in the reference. New chat defaults is below the bottom edge of the render.

accepted_deviations.as_given: The Notifications switch moved to that section: the desktop rail no longer has the "Notifications / Blocked in Settings" switch at its bottom, and the More drawer no longer has the "Notifications / Blocked in Settings" row at its end. So the drawer is shorter and its top edge sits lower.
accepted_deviations.note: The render's rail has no "Notifications / Blocked in Settings" switch at its bottom, and nothing else in the rail moved. The More drawer is closed in both pictures, so its part of this deviation cannot be seen in this frame.

limits: The side-by-side image (3048 x 1010) was shown to me scaled down to 2576 x 854, so I could not check differences under about 2 px.

Both pictures are cut at the 982 px viewport height. I could not compare the New chat defaults section, which is mostly below the edge in the reference and fully below it in the render, or anything further down.
The More drawer is closed in both pictures, so I could not check the drawer part of A3.
